Subject: EdgePod deployment — floorplan + initial questions

Hi Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. We're excited to move forward with a private Redwood deployment in Rackfield Rack-A3 (our new edge pod). I attached the floorplan and rack elevations for context (attachment: rackfield_floorplan.pdf).

High-level ask: we want guidance on cluster sizing, node classes (GPU/CPU mixes), and where model weights should live (local NVMe vs remote block storage). Some specifics from our side:
- 2x 48U racks available (A3-A4), each with dual 32A PDUs.
- Top-of-rack switches are Arista 7060CX-32S, spine is Arista 7500.
- We'll provide BGP peer for public egress if needed.
- We prefer local NVMe for hot cache, but need recommendations for persistence and cross-node replication.

Can your team propose a short checklist (network handoff, power per node, storage topology) so our colo team can prep? Also we may need a small air-gapped option for regulatory workloads.

Cheers,
Ben

Ben — thanks for the floorplan and the clear list. Looping in Marcus (runtime/infra), Priyom (provisioning) and Kimberly (security/compliance). High-level response and a proposed prep checklist below; Marcus will follow with specifics and node profiles.

Quick answers up front:
- Local NVMe: great for KV cache and transient model shards; don't rely on it for authoritative weight storage unless you have replication (we recommend network-backed block store with selective local caching).
- Node classes: separate into control/infra, compute (cpu-only), accel (gpu + nvme), and storage nodes (network-attached weight store). We prefer explicit nodeclasses to keep scheduling and eviction simple.
- Network handoff: we will need an L2 or routed L3 handoff at the ToR with dedicated VLANs for control plane, pod overlay, and model data (S3/REST + block). BGP is fine for egress; we'll provide suggested prefixes.

Prep checklist for colo team (short):
1) Confirm PDU per-rack usable power per node (include breaker trip/derating).
2) Label ToR ports and provide switch console access + allowed mgmt ACLs.
3) Decide on storage topology: LVM-localpv for hot NVMe + RBD/Ceph or iSCSI for weight store.
4) Confirm whether air-gapped workloads require separate management plane (we can provide an air-gapped package).
5) Provide a point-of-contact for lift-and-shift window and an initial maintenance blackout window.

I've attached our node profile workbook (redwood_node_profiles_v1.xlsx) — Marcus will call out exact CPU/GPU counts and storage layout. Proposed next step: 30‑minute tech sync Wednesday PST to validate power and network details.

Best,
Laura Bennett

Ben / Team — following up with concrete recommendations based on the floorplan and typical EdgePod constraints. Summary first, then the checklist of actionable items.

Summary recommendations:
- Node classes and baseline counts (start small, scale by pod):
  * control-plane: 3x r620-like (8vCPU, 64GB, 1x 480GB SSD) — HA masters (tolerates 1 failover)
  * infra: 2x (monitoring, logging, ingress) 16vCPU, 128GB, 2x1TB NVMe (mirrored)
  * compute-cpu: 6x m64 (64vCPU, 256GB, 2x1TB NVMe) for batching/CPU-only tasks
  * accel-gpu: 4x gpu-accelerators (2xA10/4xA100 depending on availability) with 8TB NVMe local cache (for kv cache + ephemeral weights)
  * storage-backend: 3x storage nodes (dual 25Gb NICs, 48TB usable via RBD or iSCSI) for model weight persistence and backups

- Storage approach:
  * Hot cache (KV/continuation cache): local NVMe, exposed via local CSI (LVM + localpv) with node affinity and fast eviction policies.
  * Persistent weights: network block store (RBD/Ceph recommended if you want replication + topology awareness; otherwise managed iSCSI/NetApp). Use VolumeBindingMode=WaitForFirstConsumer and topologyKeys to ensure PVCs land next to GPU nodes if needed.
  * Snapshot/backup: Velero + S3-compatible gateway to a locked-backup bucket (object store may be on a separate colo node or remote cloud depending on regulations).

- Network:
  * Underlay: L3 with ARP proxy disabled on ToR; use BGP EVPN if available to allow host routes for pods across racks.
  * VLANS: mgmt(10), control-plane(20), pod-overlay(30), storage(40), monitoring(50).
  * MTU: 9000 across ToR/spine for RDMA-like performance on NVMe-over-Fabrics if used.
  * Egress: BGP session to your spine with a dedicated /28 for our service egress prefixes.

- OS/kernel tuning (high level):
  * Increase net.core.rmem_max/net.core.wmem_max, tcp_tw_recycle disabled, vm.swappiness=10, set hugepages for model-serving containers when using shared memory.
  * Kubelet: --eviction-hard=nodefs.available<5%,memory.available<200Mi, set kube-reserved and system-reserved per node class.

Action checklist for colo ops (what we need from you):
1) Confirm per-node available amperage and a labeled PDU map for each cabinet.
2) Provide ToR console access and an on-call window for BGP peering test.
3) Decide whether you prefer Ceph/RBD vs iSCSI; if Ceph, supply OSD disk candidates and network VLANs for cluster traffic.
4) Confirm whether cross-node NVMe replication (NVMe-oF) is permitted — if not, we will rely on network-backed replicas for durability.
5) Provide an S3-compatible bucket endpoint (or accept our locked remote backup plan).

I'll be on the call Wednesday with Laura to walk the team through these items.

- Marcus

4) Air-gapped: we need a minimized package where control plane and registry are local; can Redwood provide an offline registry tarball and install playbook?

Short runbook we will follow on deploy day (bullet form):

2) Provision control plane on isolated VLAN and validate API server reachability.
3) Bring up storage-backend and verify replication health (if Ceph: OSDs up and placement groups active).
4) Join compute and accel nodes, run kubelet tuning script, validate CSI nodes.
5) Run simple model load test (1x small model then 1x medium) and validate KV cache eviction and weight fetch paths.
